title: Style sample: data-ledger
objective: Show what a data-ledger film looks like: one chart that draws itself, labelled on the line.
audience: The Motion Lab team, reviewing what each style template looks like before using it.

message.core_message: World population took 123 years to go from one to two billion and 11 to go from seven to eight.
key_points: Sets the scale of the story before any chart.
Makes the chart readable before it moves.
Shows that each billion arrived faster than the last.
Sets the first step against the latest one.
Lands the takeaway with its source.

constraints: Silent: no narration, music or effects; the picture carries it.
Built to style template data-ledger v2; scene roles follow its scene grammar.

research.reason: Style sample for look review, not a release. On-screen facts are a few well-established figures checked by hand; the source is named on screen. Figures: UN World Population Prospects milestones (1804, 1927, 1960, 1974, 1987, 1999, 2011, 2022).

creative_directions.name: data-ledger template
creative_directions.concept: A 22-second walk through the data-ledger template's scene grammar on a subject that fits its visual job: Each billion came faster.

composition.approach: Portrait only: copy in the top band, the hero in the middle, captions above the bottom UI zone.

creative_directions.pacing: A planned visual event at least every 2 seconds.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: It is the template's own grammar, so the sample shows the template rather than one film's choices.

success_criteria: Each scene role of the template is recognisable
No frame holds still for more than 2.5 s
